recent_posts.title: Borrow-checking without type-checking
recent_posts.summary: A deep technical exploration of implementing borrow-checking in a dynamically-typed toy language without a static type system. The author demonstrates how ownership, borrowing, and shared references can be enforced at runtime using a compact reference-counting scheme stored on the stack. Key design decisions include: using a single integer per variable to encode moved/borrowed/shared states, storing lender and owner provenance in 42 bits per reference, and scanning the stack to produce useful error messages on violations. The system supports interior pointers, stack allocation, external iterators, and closures with explicit captures. Comparisons are drawn to Rust, Hylo, Mojo, Swift, C# refs, and other ownership systems, with honest discussion of tradeoffs and remaining limitations.

recent_posts.title: 2025 year in review: conference, language design, and performance consulting
recent_posts.summary: A personal year-in-review for 2025 from an independent developer and researcher. Covers running the hytradboi online conference (481 attendees, 28 talks), progress on a hobby programming language called Zest (adding namespaces, recursion, compile-time evaluation, and grappling with novel memory management), consulting work including a ~4x median latency improvement in a Go codebase, and three published technical writings on query compilers and compilation strategies. Plans for 2026 include smaller experimental projects, reviving GitHub sponsorships, and deliberately introducing more variety and chaos after two years of over-optimization.

recent_posts.title: SQL needed structure
recent_posts.summary: SQL struggles with producing hierarchical data structures needed for modern web applications. Traditional approaches require multiple queries and complex joins to transform flat relational data into nested structures like JSON. Modern SQL features like jsonb_agg can generate structured output in a single query, reducing network roundtrips and simplifying data retrieval for UI rendering.

recent_posts.title: A consultant's measured take on LLM adoption in software development
recent_posts.summary: A software consultant shares their measured perspective on LLM adoption, observing that while clients using LLM tools showed average productivity and code quality, the tools struggled with performance optimization tasks. The author highlights concerns about cost structures, rapidly changing interfaces, and the challenge of fact-checking LLM output, while noting some promising applications in transcription, code review assistance, and assembly language explanation.

recent_posts.title: Go allocation probe
recent_posts.summary: A custom profiling tool built using bpftrace and eBPF to track Go memory allocations by type. The tool attaches uprobes to Go's mallocgc function to capture allocation data, then resolves type names by parsing ELF sections and Go's internal type system. Despite being fragile, it successfully identified performance issues caused by excessive string pointer allocations across multiple code locations.

recent_posts.title: Store tags after payloads
recent_posts.summary: Storing enum tags after payloads instead of before can significantly reduce memory usage by avoiding alignment padding. Traditional enum layout places tags first, causing alignment requirements to add padding between tag and payload fields. By reversing the order and placing tags last, nested enums can achieve much more compact memory layouts, with Swift being a notable language that implements this optimization.

top_posts.title: Digital minimalism
top_posts.summary: Digital minimalism advocates for a mindful and intentional use of technology, focusing on improving personal value and high-quality leisure time. It criticizes the addictive nature of digital media driven by the advertising industry and emphasizes the importance of solitude for mental well-being, agency, and regulating emotions. Practical advice includes prioritizing demanding activities over passive consumption and seeking real-world social interactions.

top_posts.title: The missing tier for query compilers
top_posts.summary: Query engines are facing challenges in performance due to the interpreter overhead, especially for OLTP and OLAP queries. While vectorization helps for OLAP workloads, compiled queries can significantly improve OLTP performance by reducing the overhead. However, query compilation has its trade-offs, such as unpredictable performance and compile-time delays. The post compares approaches to query compilation in databases and browsers, highlighting the pros and cons of different methods like baseline compilers and interpreters. The need for a middle tier between interpreters and full compilers is emphasized, suggesting potential solutions for more efficient query execution.
